title: Police shooting victim never violent ; Bradford man's brother was more feared, inquest told: [Ontario Edition]
article: Mark Graham may have seemed a little odd, maybe even depressed, but friends never expected him to become violent, an inquest has been told.
The testimony came on the first day of the inquest into the fatal police shooting of Graham, 38, last summer in the parking lot of a Tim Hortons in Bradford, just north of Toronto.
Debrah Fisher testified she had felt threatened by Graham, and police were called when he showed up on her doorstep that day.

When the South Simcoe police arrived, they followed Graham on foot to the parking lot, as onlookers were taunting the officers and cheering on Graham, telling him not to give up. Eventually, Graham apparently reached for a hidden sawed-off shotgun, and that's when officers shot him, the inquest was told.
But Fisher, the ex-girlfriend of Graham's brother Mike, testified that while Mark Graham drank often, in her opinion he was never violent.
Fisher had dated Mike for four months before he was charged with assault for beating her. During their turbulent relationship, Fisher said she saw his brother Mark as "a bubbly, happy type."

She recounted that on July 28, she was accompanied by her friend Raymond Tailfer at a birthday party for her daughter at a local restaurant. At some point, Tailfer was called out of the restaurant. When he returned, he told Fisher he had been shot by Mark Graham. He has since recovered. The next day, Mark Graham arrived on Fisher's apartment doorstep. She pushed her daughter out of the house, and told her to run to the corner store to call 911. While she believed that her life in danger, she insisted she did not see Mark Graham, who was unemployed, as a violent person. She admitted under cross- examination by the lawyer representing the three police officers involved in the fatal shooting that Mark Graham had threatened her previously.
In that incident, Graham- apparently siding with his brother- called her a "stool pigeon rat goof" while pointing a gun in her direction.
Yet Fisher said she was more afraid of her ex-boyfriend Mike than she was of his brother. Fisher has a restraining order against Mike, who was recently released from jail.

Fisher testified that Mike Graham, jealous of her friendship with Tailfer, had concocted a plan to kill Tailfer, Fisher and her 14- year-old son. Her ex-boyfriend had apparently discussed it with his brother in the weeks prior to the shootings, she said. Fisher also testified that Mike responded with no emotion when he learned his brother had been killed.
In fact, Mike Graham told a friend that his brother had screwed up, and now he would have to "finish the job" or kill Fisher himself, she testified.
